summary.title: False Barrels and the Road South
summary.synopsis: Returning to the Strider with phlogiston and Sedecium survivors in tow, the party briefs their allies — the Protectorate, the Scale, and the twins — on the full scope of their situation, carefully omitting their role in the Menhir's death and the Judge's true nature. They scheme to shortchange Grayson by handing off barrels of God's Blood disguised as phlogiston, then set out south toward a mysterious colorful settlement to lay low — only to find armed humanoids training rifles on them as they approach.
key_beats: The party returns to the Hesperid III where Tamara and Yao greet them at gunpoint, suspicious of the four Sedecium survivors. Johnny delivers a sweeping magical PowerPoint performance explaining the Strider's history, Machine God, Aurelia, and the Thessian threat — deliberately omitting that the party killed the Menhir and that the Judge is a Thessian. Vesper of the Scale visibly reacts to the description of 'Mr. Split' (Insuperlex).
Argyle casts Augury asking whether the party should continue killing Thessians; the result is 'wheel' (yes), which Bishop of the Scale takes as divine endorsement and agrees to ally with the party.

Benny pilots the Sedecium spaceship back to the Strider with a flawless reflex check (38). Machine God has dramatically refurbished the Undercroft — organized hallways, repaired elevators, and transformed the approach to his chamber into an ornate golden gothic pavilion with murals of the original Six.
Tamara and Yao meet Machine God. Yao, a devout member of the Iridescent Church, is starstruck to meet a living relic who knew Aurelia the First and begins asking endless questions.

Argyle stays behind at Pilgrim's Way and experiences a mystical vertigo; a glint draws his eye to the ceiling fresco — first to Honorsworn plunging his sword into an obscured enemy, then to Aurelia depicted mid-shout, seemingly communicating with her party.

The twins Anouk and Anaïs reveal they know of Sedecium through Ranka. They agree to research converting phlogiston into heart energy to help the party avoid tithes. Argyle attempts Speak with Stones on the Menhir, discovering the stones are always talking — they ARE the Menhir, not ordinary rocks.
The party consults Osyluth (the skull), who explains how to start the Strider: dock the phlogiston barrel on the lift, prime it, and hit go. The Strider is oriented toward the Voidsong.
Anzu etches custom runes onto party members: Rune of Whetstones (persistent bleed) on Benny's falcata and Rune of Appeal (+2 status to Deception, Diplomacy, Performance) on Johnny's forearm.

At a summit with Grayson, Stoke, and Manus, the party claims to have found 8 barrels of phlogiston (they actually have 15). Grayson demands the barrels be held at neutral ground and insists on sending his own people to find more. The party agrees to split: 3 barrels to Grayson's coalition, 2 to the Church, 3 to themselves.

The party fills five empty barrels with God's Blood from Galzu's tank, disguised to pass as phlogiston, and drops them at Giacomo's for pickup by the Church and Grayson's representatives. They then decide to drive south to the settlement Jethro spotted, pretending to search for more fuel.

After a four-hour uneventful drive through the wasteland, the party approaches a colorful walled settlement with massive orange, blue, and yellow tent structures. Humanoid figures on the walls aim long rifles at the approaching vehicle. Session ends here.
summary.cliffhanger: The party drives toward a colorful walled settlement in the southern wasteland, only to find armed humanoid figures on the walls aiming long rifles at their approaching vehicle.
